finding: For every number field and actual continuous idele-class character χ with unit norm, the net of partial products of the inverse evaluated χ.localPolynomial factors converges uniformly on each closed half-plane a ≤ Re(s), a > 1, to the existing finiteHeckeCharacterEulerProduct χ. A summable majorant, independent of s in that set, bounds the absolute deviations from 1, giving absolute convergence at every Re(s) > 1. The opening notation gives no proof; Lemma 3.2.1.1 refers to comparison with the Riemann zeta Euler product. The Lean proof uses an existing summable residue-norm bound from ideal counting, uniform summability of the principal logarithms, and a common upper bound on the real parts of their sum to exponentiate uniformly. The existing finiteHecke_localPolynomial_eval_uniformizer and finiteHeckeEulerFactor_eq_one_of_ramified identify the literal local factors, and completedHeckeEulerProduct multiplies the same finite term by the finite Archimedean Gamma product. This is finite-place convergence and its attachment in the defining completed product, not identification with another L-function or convergence of a completed partial-product net uniformly on the unbounded half-plane. It does not assert convergence on the 1-line, continuation, or a zero-location result.
